title: Birth in Charleston and Dafts Court
summary: Greene gives his birth date and describes the court off Rutledge Avenue where he was born and lived until 1923.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: PROCEEDINGS

Helen and Stanley Dance are interviewing Freddie Green
August 9, 1977.
Freddie, we want to ask you where and when you were born and we want you to digress at length about your background. So, when were you?
I was born on March 31, 1911, in Charleston, South Carolina. It's a place on Rutledge Avenue.
Rutledge?
Rutledge.
Yeah.
And there's a court there called Dafts Court. It's -- about twelve houses.
How do you spell Dafts?
D-A-L-T-S. And, there's twelve houses on it, and I was born in one of them -- number 7, Dafts Court.
Yeah, number 7, Dafts Court. That was maybe -- kind of nice -- to be in a court rather than on the street?
Yeah -- it's a court with twelve -- right off of Rutledge Avenue.
Now Charleston is very pretty isn't it? We drove into it this year and it's very pretty.
Yes, it's a beautiful place -- a beautiful city.
So was it nice, shady trees and everything?
Well, they had trees, -- yes.
Yeah.
There's alot of trees around there.
Yeah. Where is Rutledge? Does it run right through the center of town or where does it run?
Yes. It runs right through the center of town. It's one of the main streets there in Charleston, and this is right between -- there's two streets in between, which is Race and Rutledge --
Yeah.
Race and something-or-other -- along Rutledge.
I see.
And right in the middle is this court called DaIts Court.
That's nice. How long had the family lived there?
Well, let's see. I lived there until 1923, and then came to New York.
You did?
Yes.
So the whole first part of your life you lived there?
Yes.
